title: Class teacher, secondary department
summary: Lead a class of eight Key Stage 4 pupils on our Discoverers pathway, supported by an experienced team of three teaching assistants.
about: We're looking for a teacher who enjoys planning practical, hands-on lessons and who sees each pupil's EHCP as a working document rather than paperwork.

You don't need to have worked in a special school before. We care more about how you build relationships with young people and how willing you are to learn from the therapists, families and support staff around you.
responsibilities: Plan and teach a broad curriculum adapted to each pupil's communication and learning needs
Lead and deploy a team of teaching assistants
Write and review termly targets linked to pupils' EHCP outcomes
Contribute to annual reviews and keep families informed of progress
Work alongside speech and language and occupational therapists
personSpecification: Experience of adapting teaching for pupils with additional needs
Calm, consistent approach to supporting behaviour
Willingness to complete Team Teach training
Commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children

title: Teaching assistant (level 3)
hours: 32.5 hours a week, term time only
summary: Support pupils in our primary department with learning, communication and personal care.
about: Our teaching assistants are at the centre of school life. You'll work closely with one class team and get to know each pupil well.
Full training is provided, including Makaton, moving and handling, and medical procedures where needed.
responsibilities: Support small group and one-to-one learning planned by the class teacher
Help pupils with personal care, eating and mobility
Use visual supports, Makaton and communication aids
Record observations and progress towards targets
personSpecification: Level 3 qualification in supporting teaching and learning, or equivalent experience
Experience working with children or young people with additional needs
Patient, warm and good at staying calm
Commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children

title: Midday supervisor
hours: 7.5 hours a week, 11:45am to 1:15pm, term time only
summary: Help pupils enjoy a calm, sociable lunchtime, both in the dining hall and on the playground.
about: A good role for someone who wants a few hours' work in the middle of the day. Lunchtimes are an important part of our pupils' day for social skills and independence.
responsibilities: Support pupils at lunch, including those who need help with eating
Lead simple playground games and activities
Follow pupils' care and behaviour plans
personSpecification: Experience of caring for children, paid or unpaid
Kind, reliable and happy to be outdoors in all weathers
Commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children
